title: C482/946/2013 of Deepa Rani Bharti Vs Dr. Anand Prakash Sexena

paras.text:
1
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT
NAINITAL
Criminal Misc. Application No. 946 of 2013
(Under Section 482 Cr.P.C.)
Deepa Rani Bharti .............. Applicant

versus
Dr. Anand Prakash Saxena .......... Respondent
Mr. Karan Anand, Advocate, present for the applicant.
None is present for the respondent.
U.C. Dhyani, J. (Oral)
 The applicant, by means of present application
under Section 482 Cr.P.C., seek to quash the summoning
order dated 09.08.2010 and 12.01.2011 as well as the entire
proceedings of Criminal Complaint Case No. 667 of 2012
(old no. 1232 of 2010), Anand Saxena vs. Deepa Rani Bharti,
under Section 131 of the Negotiable Instruments Act,
pending before the Special Judicial Magistrate-1, Dehradun.
2. The applicant has been summoned to face the trial
for the offence punishable under Section 138 of the N.I. Act.
It is the submission of learned counsel for the applicant that
the applicant has already refunded a sum of Rs. 20 lacs to the
respondent.
3. It will be relevant to quote para 7 of the petition
herein below for convenience:

2
"That as assured by the applicant to opposite party
she refunded the aforesaid amount by way of
demand draft no. 150661 dated 12.10.2009
amounting Rs. 2,00,000/- (two lacs) to the opposite
party. A true copy of the demand draft no. 150661
dated 12.10.2009 amounting Rs. 2,00,000/- drawn at
ICICI Bank Ltd. is being filed herewith and marked
as Annexure no.1 to this affidavit."
4. Notice was sent to the respondent but none has
appeared for him despite service of notice. It appears that the
respondent is not interested in contesting the petition under
Section 482 Cr.P.C.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that if
the petitioner is asked to face the trial, the same will amount
to abuse of process of the Court.
6. When the petition was taken up for admission in
the year 2013, an interim stay was granted in favour of the
applicant.
7. Learned counsel for the applicants placed the
judgment rendered by Hon'ble Apex Court in D.P.Gulati vs.
State of Uttar Pradesh and others, reported in 2015 0
AIR(SC) 3760 to emphasis that power under Section 482
Cr.P.C. should be exercised to prevent abuse of process of
law and to secure the ends of justice.
8. This court finds substance in the submission of
learned counsel for the applicants that if the trial against the
applicants continues, the same may amount to abuse of the

3
process of the Court. In such a situation, it will be a futile
exercise to keep the criminal case pending against the
applicant.
9. The Constitutional Bench of the Hon'ble Apex
Court in the decision of Inder Mohan Gosami and another
vs. State of Uttararanhal and others, reported in (2008) 1
SCC (Cri.) 259, has laid down the guidelines for exercising
the powers under section 482 Cr.P.C., wherein it was held
that inherent power under section 482 Cr.P.C. can been
exercised:
i. to give effect to an order under the Code;
ii. to prevent abuse of the process of the court, and
iii. to otherwise secure the ends of justice.
10. In view of the above discussion, C-482 Petition is
allowed. Accordingly, the summoning orders dated
09.08.2010 and 12.01.2011 as well as the entire proceedings
of Criminal Complaint Case No. 667 of 2012 (old no. 1232
of 2010), Anand Saxena vs. Deepa Rani Bharti, under
Section 131 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, pending
before the Special Judicial Magistrate-1, Dehradun, are
hereby set aside qua applicant.
11. Since present C-482 Cr.P.C. petition is being
decided in the absence of respondent, although with due
notice, still liberty is granted to him to move for recall of this
Order, if he feels aggrieved with the same.
 (U.C.Dhyani,J.)
 25.07.2017
Kaushal
